what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: A clause that joins inertia with the rule's pair weights. SETTING (blocks 44-47; open PRs titled 'ail44: records with inertia', 'ail45: the wind law', 'ail46: the potential of the wind', 'ail47: transparent bodies'): a supplied clause, not adopted: a record's content is its direction of travel (sphere menu: a record with unit vector s steps to x + e_k with probability max(0, s.e_k)/sqrt 3; an occupied target exchanges contents; bonds re-draw their pair of contents uniformly on the momentum class at rate gamma); bodies are sets of solid sites that CAPTURE the records stepping onto them. ESTABLISHED: number and momentum conserved locally; uniform stationary measure; pressure rho/(3 sqrt 3), wave speed sqrt(1 - rho)/3; a body capturing Q per tick draws the wind g = sqrt3 Q/(4 pi r^2 (1 - rho)) (executed to 1-3 per cent), the wind of several bodies is the superposition of their potential flows (executed: fit coefficient 0.983-0.998, residual = noise); two capturing bodies attract with F = K Q1 Q2/r^2, K -> K_0 = sqrt3/(4 pi rho (1 - rho)) at low density and for dilute bodies; a capturing site takes up q_1 = (sqrt 3/2) rho per tick (executed 0.236-0.241 against 0.251 at rho = 0.29) and a body captures through its exposed faces; for bodies TRANSPARENT to the gas the force is G N1 N2/r^2 with G = 3 sqrt3 rho/(16 pi (1 - rho)) (executed at separation 16, rho = 0.3, gamma = 1: F/(N1 N2) = (1.44 +- 0.10)e-4 against 1.46e-4). COSTS, not yet executed: the same rate q_1 makes bodies grow and drags their motion towards the local wind; the supervisor's estimate is that attraction outruns both only when the gas inside an orbit weighs much less than the central body, about (4 pi/3) rho r^3 << N/6. Simulators in probes/lib: inertial.py, inertial_bodies.py, inertial_porous_bodies.py (usage: L rho0 sep ticks seed gamma R1 f1 R2 f2; a ball of radius R with each site solid with probability f; f2 = 0 for a single body), inertial_superposition.py. TASK: block 44's inertial clause ignores the admissibility rule's pair weights omega = (p, q, r) between neighbouring records' contents; blocks 39-40 had records moving by pair weights without inertia (equilibrium = the static law on the occupied set). (a) Propose covariant clauses that have both: streaming along contents with number and momentum conserved, and a stationary law that is the law with vacancies of block 39 (or show that none exists with nearest-neighbour events). Known obstacle: streaming changes which records are adjacent, so the weight changes along a move, and a driven (irreversible) dynamics does not in general keep a Gibbs measure stationary; find the rate conditions (pairwise balance) under which it does, or prove impossibility for the six-axis menu on Z^3. (b) If a clause exists, compute its product-state-like currents and pressure to first order in (omega - constant) and say whether the wind law survives. (c) If none exists, give the closest clause (e.g. weights acting only in the scattering step) and its stationary law on small windows. check.py: exact stationarity check on the 3^3 torus with two records, as in block 44's runner.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/inertia-with-the-rules-weights/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
